headline: High Wind Warning issued as southern New England storm arrives
dek: The National Weather Service expects 45-to-60-mph gusts, power outages and coastal flooding across eastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island through the weekend.
body: The National Weather Service Boston/Norton office has upgraded the coastal storm threat to a High Wind Warning for eastern, northeastern and southeastern Massachusetts and northern and southern Rhode Island. The warning runs from 8 a.m. Friday to 2 a.m. Sunday and includes Boston, Plymouth, New Bedford, Newport, Narragansett and Nantucket.

Forecasters expect northeast winds of 25 to 35 mph, with gusts of 45 to 60 mph. The NWS says damaging winds could bring down branches and power lines, with power outages expected and travel potentially difficult for high-profile vehicles.

Coastal hazards are also escalating. The NWS lists coastal-flood warnings, advisories or watches for parts of Massachusetts and Rhode Island, depending on location, and a High Surf Advisory remains in effect through Sunday evening. Breaking waves could reach 6 to 17 feet, creating dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

The long duration of the winds, heavy rain and fully leafed trees could increase the risk of tree damage and outages, according to the NWS. Conditions and alert levels may differ by community as the storm moves north along the coast.

Residents in vulnerable coastal areas, boaters and weekend travelers should secure loose objects and monitor updated forecasts and local emergency notices. The warnings describe expected hazards, but impacts will not be identical everywhere.
author: NorthEast News Desk
